Provenance, not blended with any earlier layer's: Opus 169dd1 copied the old values from the 43594eba Root text before any producer edit and wrote the new literals in the same pass; they were NOT approved before it, and their independent review is the Fable scoped review requested for this amendment bundle, which this file does not record. amendments.old: Only on an explicit operator request, reopen ONE DORMANT pi, pi-durable or Claude Code citizen under its OWN garden id, in a visible window in the operator's own tmux session — or, for pi or pi-durable inside herdr, a new herdr tab. The record supplies everything — which session, which cwd, and for pi which transcript, model and provider — so the only input is the target id: there is no model override, no task, and no prompt, and a Claude Code session comes back as `claude --resume <its session id>` with none of the model or permission flags it was once started with. This verb submits NO prompt; what the runtime itself does after it comes back (for Claude Code, its hook re-arms the doorbell and unread mail may then wake a turn) is not measured, and talking to it is still entwurf_v2 fire-and-forget. You get TWO receipts and they mean different things: a LAUNCH receipt (tmux made a window, or herdr a tab, and was asked to start the runtime) and an OBSERVATION receipt (pi: the control socket answered under the same id; pi-durable: the child it started adopted this call's reservation; Claude Code: a NEW live process in the window this call opened re-armed its receiver marker for the same session with a fresh arm binding the record also carries; or resume-unobserved; or record-unreadable with its cause). Unobserved is a real outcome, not an error to retry — the window is visible, so read it. A citizen that is already LIVE is refused: address it with entwurf_v2 instead. A Claude Code citizen is reopened only when the last validated owner the Entwurf hook armed for its session is proven gone AND that arm is still the record's last one; no marker, an unreadable or mismatched one, an inconclusive owner or an unbound one is refused, and a process holding the session without a committed hook attach is invisible to that proof. Other backends have no same-id resume. Requires that this agent itself runs inside tmux, or inside herdr for a pi or pi-durable target (a Claude Code target is refused there, never sent to tmux).
amendments.new: Only on an explicit operator request, reopen ONE DORMANT pi, pi-durable or Claude Code citizen under its OWN garden id, in a visible window in the operator's own tmux session — or, for pi or pi-durable inside herdr, a new herdr tab. The record supplies session, cwd and, for pi, the transcript's model and provider; the only input is the target id (no model override, task or prompt). Claude Code returns as `claude --resume <session id>` without its earlier model or permission flags. This verb submits NO prompt; what the runtime does once back (for Claude Code, unread mail may wake a turn) is not measured; talking to it is still entwurf_v2 fire-and-forget. TWO receipts mean different things: a LAUNCH receipt (a tmux window or herdr tab was made and asked to start the runtime) and an OBSERVATION receipt (pi: the control socket answered under the same id; pi-durable: the started child adopted this call's reservation (not readiness), or not-yet-adopted / reservation-lost; Claude Code: a NEW live process in this call's window re-armed the session's marker with a fresh binding in the record; or resume-unobserved, or record-unreadable with its cause). Unobserved is an outcome, not an error to retry; read the visible window. A session a live process holds is refused: a running citizen is reached only via entwurf_v2's rail check; an unadopted pi-durable reservation is not reachable by entwurf_v2. pi-durable reopens only if its session claim is closed and released or its holder is proven gone. Claude Code reopens only if the last validated owner its Entwurf hook armed is proven gone AND that arm is still the record's last; a missing, unreadable, mismatched or unbound marker or an inconclusive owner refuses, and a session held without a committed hook attach is invisible to that proof. Other backends have no same-id resume. This agent itself must run inside tmux, or inside herdr for a pi or pi-durable target (Claude Code is refused there, never sent to tmux).

amendments.old: Only on an explicit operator request, reopen ONE dormant pi, pi-durable or Claude Code citizen under its own garden id in a visible tmux window — or, for pi or pi-durable inside herdr, a new herdr tab — through the entwurf-bridge (target required; the record supplies the session and cwd — no task or prompt is submitted). Returns the bridge's LAUNCH and OBSERVATION receipts or its named refusal: a live target, another backend, or a Claude Code citizen not proven dormant is refused by name, and opening it needs the tmux session — or, for pi or pi-durable only, the herdr pane — this host itself was launched in; a Claude Code target inside herdr is refused, never sent to tmux. Existing unread mail may still wake the resumed runtime; neither receipt proves what it did.
amendments.new: Only on an explicit operator request, reopen ONE dormant pi, pi-durable or Claude Code citizen under its own garden id in a visible tmux window — or, for pi or pi-durable inside herdr, a new herdr tab — through the entwurf-bridge (target required; the record supplies the session and cwd — no task or prompt is submitted). Returns the bridge's LAUNCH and OBSERVATION receipts or its named refusal: a session a live process holds (a running citizen, or a pi-durable reservation awaiting adoption), another backend, or a citizen not proven dormant is refused by name, and opening it needs the tmux session — or, for pi or pi-durable only, the herdr pane — this host itself was launched in; a Claude Code target inside herdr is refused, never sent to tmux. Existing unread mail may still wake the resumed runtime; neither receipt proves what it did.

amendments.old: CANONICAL DELIVERY SURFACE for garden ids: message, reply, or hand off to whoever an id names. The id alone does not say which rail that citizen answers on. Give target + intent; the decider picks transport from liveness (live socket citizen → control-socket send; deliverable self-fetch citizen → meta-bridge mailbox; probe-alive native-push citizen → direct injection into its conversation) and reports ONE outcome, named per rail: a control receiver's acceptance boundary (`sent` / `queued-steer` / `queued-follow-up` / `accepted-unknown-boundary` — those four, or `mailbox-enqueued` on a re-resolved mailbox leg), a mailbox ENQUEUE receipt, a native-push INJECTION, a rejection, or lock-dirty. This receipt is not the colleague's reply or evidence of reading. EXISTING targets only; discover with entwurf_peers. A live socket can receive fire-and-forget. unsupported means only "no control-socket probe," not reachability. The decider resolves the actual rail at dispatch time: a self-fetch mailbox only while deliverable, native-push direct injection only while its adapter probe is alive, or a THIRD RESULT: rejection when neither holds. An inactive self-fetch citizen is mailbox-undeliverable; native-push has NO mailbox: dead → native-push-target-dead; indeterminate → native-push-probe-indeterminate; agy (paused, #152) → native-push-paused, no probe. A dormant socket rejects this delivery verb as dormant-fire-forget-unsupported. owned-outcome was withdrawn. Only on an explicit operator request, entwurf_resume_call may visibly reopen a proven-dormant Pi or Claude Code citizen under the same id, submitting no prompt; that lifecycle is separate from delivery. LOCK: taken for a control-socket-DOMAIN dispatch. The mailbox and native-push rails are lock-free — deliverability and the adapter probe guard them. mode applies to a CONTROL-SOCKET send only; other plans carry no mode. wants_reply rides every rail. message caps at 16000 chars; send an artifact path + digest for more.

amendments.old: List the entwurf fact surface: garden citizens (from meta-records) with their liveness, plus diagnostics. The record is the sole address axis — a control socket no record claims is a `record-less-socket` diagnostic (a stale/diagnostic state), never a peer row. This reports FACTS, never verbs: `liveness` is a fact (alive/dead/indeterminate, or `unsupported` for a backend with no control-socket probe such as claude-code); the delivery choice or rejection is resolved LATER by entwurf_v2 from the record and current rail facts, not here — this surface carries no per-row routing field, so do not read a transport off a row. A `dead` socket row is a REPORTED FACT: no entwurf_v2 delivery is available while it is dormant. Listing it grants no action and is not an invitation to dispatch. Only on an explicit operator request, the separate entwurf_resume_call may visibly reopen a proven-dormant Pi or Claude Code citizen under the same id, submitting no prompt. In particular `unsupported` does NOT mean mailbox: it means this backend has no control-socket probe. Dispatch has THREE possible answers — a self-fetch mailbox (only while that mailbox is deliverable), native-push direct injection (only while its adapter probe is alive), or a REJECT when neither holds: mailbox-undeliverable for a self-fetch citizen whose inbox nobody drains, and on the native-push probe dead → native-push-target-dead vs indeterminate → native-push-probe-indeterminate, kept apart because an unestablished probe is not a departed host; an agy target rejects as native-push-paused (#152) without being probed. Note: this is the *active* world and it is facts-only — it creates nothing. Pass an existing garden id to entwurf_v2; to open a NEW sibling use entwurf_fresh_call.
